_doc: The questions the harness-setup skill asks, in order. `when` is a Python expression over the earlier answers; a question whose `when` is false is skipped and its answer dropped. `default` may be a plain value or {by: <answer id>, values: {...}, else: ...}. `example` feeds `build.py --example`.

questions.prompt: What is the project called? (shown in CLAUDE.md and the board header)
Which version control does the project use?

options.label: git (branches, worktrees, pull requests with gh)
Subversion (^/trunk, ^/branches, working copies next to the checkout, landing through sv.py)

questions.prompt: Name of the main line (git: master or main)

options.label: Single user: one person, one supervisor session, no coordinator sessions
Multi-user: several developers, each with a coordinator session next to the one supervisor

questions.prompt: Your name as written in task files (the supervisor's user and default task owner; one word)
Everyone who answers questions and owns tasks, including you (one word each, comma separated)

options.label: Open: anyone may refine, start-approve and answer any task and change its owner (owner = creator and addressee, no special rights)
Strict: the owner decides a task's questions, plan and start; only the current owner transfers it; a coordinator acts on its dev's tasks only

questions.prompt: Is there data whose numbers can change with a code change (computed values, scores, stored rows)? Then the harness adds the analyst agent and asks reviewers to measure data impact before/after.

options.label: Deploy to production and check the production data or behaviour
Deploy to a test server and verify there; production releases are separate ops tasks
No deployment: a landed task goes straight to 07-Done

questions.prompt: Task types (comma separated; keep research and ops, they have their own flow and meaning)
Board colour 1, the primary (buttons, links), as #rrggbb
Board colour 2, the accent (badges, highlights), as #rrggbb
Port of the local web board
The command that runs Python 3.10+ in this project (python, python3, py -3, a venv path)
What must never end up in versioned files, commit messages or agent reports? (one line; it goes into the confidentiality rules)
questions.default: host names, IP addresses, credentials, customer data and private file names

example.git: host names, IP addresses, trading-course or methodology names, private file names (P__*, PRIVATE_*) and credentials
example.svn: host names, credentials, passwords and customer files
